A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MOTIP, with identifiable correspondence between methods, experiments and appendix material. All 28 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2 were readable, including equations, tables and figures; the extensive revision does not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original MOTIP benchmark results, ablations, ID-shuffling experiments and inference-speed measurements in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark results, including BFT, revised ablations and inference-speed measurements in Section 4 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The core detector, ID dictionary and decoder architecture remain; v2 Appendix D.5 explicitly states that the model structure is unchanged. However, default inference changes from Hungarian matching in v1 Appendix A.2 to per-object maximum-score predictions with duplicate-ID resolution in v2 Section 3.4 and Appendix B.2.

E1.justification: V2 adds training and evaluation on BFT, covering 22 bird species and highly dynamic nonhuman tracking. This substantially extends the represented population beyond human tracking. DanceTrack, SportsMOT and MOT17 remain covered, with MOT17 relocated to Appendix D.1.

E2.justification: V2 replaces v1's cosine-supervised comparator with FairMOT-style identity-classification training and adds ReID variants controlling for Hungarian assignment and trajectory-module capacity. Benchmark comparisons also change: StrongSORT and DiffMOT are added on DanceTrack, while Hybrid-SORT-ReID and MeMOTR+ from v1 Table 9 disappear. These are substantive comparator changes, beyond relocated rows.

E3.justification: Reported DanceTrack/SportsMOT history lengths change from 39/39 to 29/59, training epochs from 14/18 to 10/13, and the default ID-switch augmentation probability from 0.3 to 0.5. Ablations become DanceTrack-only. Speed evaluation changes from RTX 4090 FP32 to RTX A5000 with FP32 and FP16. These are explicit setting revisions, not merely newly disclosed details.

E4.justification: V2 adds a decoder-depth sweep and expands self-attention and ReID analyses with Hungarian-assignment, augmentation and matched-module controls. It replaces the SportsMOT augmentation sweep with a DanceTrack study and removes the one-hot embedding comparison, shuffled-ID robustness study and DAB-DETR variant analysis. The attention visualization retains the same underlying case.

E5.justification: V1 Section 4.4 and Table 8 report 20 randomized ID-assignment trials with minimum, maximum, mean and standard deviation. V2 removes this entire statistical analysis without a replacement. These trials vary inference-time ID prompts; they are not repeated training runs or seed estimates.

E6.justification: Reported MOTIP HOTA changes from 67.5 to 69.6 on DanceTrack without extra data, 71.9 to 72.6 on SportsMOT, and 59.2 to 59.3 on MOT17; BFT adds 70.5. Comparator values also change, including extra-data DanceTrack MOTRv3 HOTA from 70.4 to 68.3. Revised settings and code prevent interpreting the MOTIP differences as controlled same-setting gains. Numerous ablation results are added or removed.

T1.justification: The ID dictionary, concatenated tracklet representation and classification-loss formulation remain mathematically equivalent. V2 condenses equations and explains arbitrary in-context labels more explicitly, but introduces no substantive new theorem, proof or derivation.

C1.justification: The central contribution—formulating association as in-context ID prediction—remains. V2 strengthens the conclusion from impressive benchmark performance to surpassing state of the art 'on all benchmarks'. V1 explicitly qualified its headline claims for MOT17 and crowded scenes; v2 retains the MOT17 qualification in the appendix.

C2.justification: V2 substantially develops the explanation of generalization to unseen identities and attributes limited Hungarian-matching benefits to learned assignment capabilities. Its MOT17 discussion emphasizes insufficient training diversity and heuristic priors, whereas v1 emphasized detector limitations and missing motion estimation. V2 also introduces ID-dictionary capacity as an explicit crowded-scene limitation.

D1.justification: V2 adds assignment pseudocode, explicit C=256 and input dimensions, expanded ReID implementation descriptions, BFT training schedules and stated checkpoint availability. Conversely, v1's AdamW optimizer, initial learning rate, weight decay and detailed MOT17 training/inference settings are no longer specified. Reproducibility information is substantially revised, with both additions and losses.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands coverage of newer literature, including DiffMOT, SAMBA, NetTrack and contrastive transformer tracking. Section 2 also sharpens the distinction between learning motion or appearance features and learning the final association decision, extending v1's positioning against detection-based and query-based trackers.

P1.justification: The introduction and method narrative are extensively rewritten around the unseen-identity classification problem. Training and inference become separate subsections, limitations receive a main-text section, and the appendices are reorganized. MOT17 and attention analysis move to the appendix. The author list also replaces Yijun Zhang with Ji Qi.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout and substantially restructures tables and figures. V2 replaces the opening pipeline comparison with an ID-label example, adds augmentation and pseudocode figures, redraws the architecture diagram, and expands the retained attention example. Extra-data benchmark results are consolidated into main-text tables.

improvement.justification: BFT evaluation and the stronger ReID/assignment controls provide better evidence for applicability beyond human tracking and for the central ID-prediction formulation. The expanded explanation and inference pseudocode improve clarity. The net gain is limited by removal of ID-shuffling statistics and important reproducibility settings, alongside the conclusion's insufficiently qualified 'all benchmarks' claim despite the acknowledged MOT17 gap.
